newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit extends gains but off highs vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit extends gains but off highs vs dollar.

text.p: The ringgit extended its firmness against the dollar but was off intraday highs as operators took the opportunity to buy back cheaper dollars, dealers said.

The pullback in the ringgit reflected a retreat in the Thai baht, they said. "Trading in the regionals mirrored that of the baht today. When the baht fell back, the others followed," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
The baht had rallied sharply in the morning as sentiment brightened on prospects of International Monetary Fund (IMF) credit lines for Thailand.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6220/50 to a dollar. It earlier hit a high of 2.6170.
Dealers said the ringgit was helped by continued nervousness about possible imposition of capital controls after Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's veiled threats on Monday.
Mahathir's comment about unspecified punitive actions against currency speculators triggered a selloff in dollar/ringgit, pushing it down 300 points.
Stop-loss dollar sales and thin volumes aided the ringgit's rise, dealers said.
They said the ringgit was likely to stay firm in the next few days on month-end demand and continued uncertainty over the possible curbs.
There was talk that offshore parties have started to square out their long dollar positions, dealers added.
